previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and coronary artery disease was admitted for acute shortness of breath. The symptom was attributed to fluid overload, likely due to interruption of his home diuretic (torsemide) after a recent gout admission and the salt-retaining effects of a prednisone taper. Initial concern for pulmonary embolism or heart failure was mitigated by a normal troponin, non-diagnostic D-dimer, and chest X-ray showing only minimal pulmonary vascular congestion. Renal function was stable relative to baseline, with a creatinine of 2.4 on admission improving to 2.1 at discharge. The transplant kidney ultrasound was stable with a new benign-appearing cyst. He responded well to IV furosemide and was discharged on his prior diuretic regimen with instructions to follow up in primary care and nephrology.

# DVT:
# Left knee pain:
Patient presented with persistent left knee pain for several 
days. Described as similar in nature to prior episodes of right 
knee pain, for which he was admitted previously and diagnosed 
with gout. On examination, there was overlying erythema and 
focal tenderness proximal and lateral to the patella. However, 
there was also swelling of the left calf, greater than the 
right. Synovial fluid analysis in the ED was negative for septic 
arthritis and crystal arthropathy. Bilateral lower extremity US 
Doppler showed deep venous thrombosis in the distal left lower 
extremity at the level of the peroneal veins. Patient was 
commenced on a heparin drip and bridged to warfarin, with 
significant improvement in left knee pain, although not complete 
resolution. He was commenced on a lidocaine patch, which 
provided great relief and freedom to mobilize. INR became 
supratherapeutic at 3.6 on ___, likely secondary to 
inhibition of warfarin metabolism with azithromycin use. He 
received 1mg of warfarin on ___, with INR of 3.3 on ___. He will 
be discharged home on warfarin 1 mg daily to be taken until 
___ when he is scheduled for follow-up visit with his PCP 
and INR check.

# Lower lobe pneumonia:
# Fluid overload/Pulmonary edema:
On admission, patient was experiencing shortness of breath, with 
associated orthopnea. Recent admission with fluid overload and 
dyspnea attributed to fluid retention secondary to prednisone. 
On examination, patient had increased work of breathing, an 
elevated JVP to the mastoid, and bibasilar crackles. BNP was 
elevated at 6263. Initial CXR showed likely interstitial edema 
and patient responded well to IV furosemide. Echo demonstrated 
mild symmetric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal 
global/regional systolic function. He was transitioned to PO 
torsemide 20mg daily prior to discharge. Incidentally, repeat 
CXR on ___, highlighted an area of focal consolidation 
concerning for pneumonia. Patient denied cough, sputum 
production and fevers. He was commenced on a five day course of 
ceftriaxone and azithromycin, which finished on ___ prior to 
discharge. Remained asymptomatic, except for shortness of 
breath, and afebrile throughout admission.

# ___:
Patient was admitted with a creatinine of 2.9, which appeared to 
elevated from a baseline ~2.5. Initial concern for pre-renal 
etiology due to recent admission with ___ felt secondary to 
over-diuresis. However, in the setting of volume overload, 
impaired kidney function more likely secondary to venous 
congestion. The decision was made to hold irbesartan and trend 
creatinine following IV diuresis. Creatinine improved daily and 
was 2.2 on discharge. Irbesartan was held at discharge; whether 
or not to restart this medication is deferred to the outpatient 
setting. 

# GERD:
Patient has a history of GERD, for which he is prescribed 
pantroprazole 40mg daily at home. Ongoing issues with 'chest 
soreness' since admission. Pain did not sound cardiac in nature. 
However, given his past cardiac history, EKGs were performed on 
numerous occasions; these showed no concerning signs of 
ischemia. The patient had a good response with calcium 
carbonate, Maalox and increased frequency of home pantoprazole 
(twice daily), with no complaints at discharge. Discharged on 
BID PPI with instructions to take on an empty stomach without 
other antacids to maximize absorption. He was not discharged on 
calcium carbonate/Tums (due to reflex acidity with this 
medication) or on Maalox (due to concerns over interference with 
the absorption of other meds).

===============

monitored daily, remaining stable throughout admission

# Hypertension:

isosorbide mononitrate. Irbesartan was held in the setting of 
___ and not restarted at discharged. In the setting of holding 
irbesartan, patient was hypertension with systolics in the 
140s-160s. Amlodipine was increased to 10 mg daily from 5 mg. 
Encourage further consideration of increased intensity of 
antihypertensive regimen as an outpatient. 

# T2DM:
Continued home glargine with an insulin sliding scale while 
inpatient. Blood glucose levels remained well controlled.

# Normocytic anemia:
Baseline hemoglobin appears to lie between 11.5 and 12. On 
admission, patient had a hemoglobin of 10.3. There was no 
evidence of bleeding, and the decision was made to trend the 
hemoglobin with transfusion if it dropped below 7. On discharge, 
hemoglobin was 10.5.
